Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2 y + 9 z &=-12 \\ 2 x - y + 9 z &=-12 \\ - 2 x + 4 y - 18 z &=24\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 9 & -12 \\ 2 & -1 & 9 & -12 \\ -2 & 4 & -18 & 24\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 9 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ -2 & 4 & -18 & 24\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 9 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 9 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2 x - y + 9 z &=-12 \\ x - y + 6 z &=-8 \\ 2 y - 6 z &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -1 & 9 & -12 \\ 1 & -1 & 6 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 6 & -8 \\ 2 & -1 & 9 & -12 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 6 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 6 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 z &=-4 \\ y - 3 z &=4 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=- 3 z - 4 \\ y &=3 z + 4 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}- 3 z - 4 \\ 3 z + 4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
